candidates.locator: page 31, section fact_sheet, table column headers
candidates.exact_span:
POLLUTANTS                   CAS No.     STORET   Domestic   Irrigation   or Wildlife   Aquatic    Aquatic     Health     Max Conc    Avg Conc      Total       Total    Max Load    Avg Load
                                                   Limits     Limits        Limits      Limits      Limits     Limits       ug/l        ug/l        ug/l        ug/l      Ib/day      Ib/day
candidates.computation_change_reason: The table defines multiple parallel limit categories (domestic, irrigation, livestock/wildlife, acute/chronic aquatic, human health, concentration vs. load, daily max vs. monthly average). Which column represents the enforceable discharge limit for a given measurement depends on how these headers are read against the facility's receiving water and reporting basis; that choice changes applicable-limit selection (A) and whether a missing or non-numeric result can be compared at all (C).

candidates.locator: page 31, section fact_sheet, pollutants table, Aldrin row
candidates.computation_change_reason: Numeric values appear only under human-health and concentration/load columns while aquatic and use-specific columns are N/A. Interpreting which of the listed ug/l or lb/day figures is the operative enforceable limit—and whether aquatic limits are absent or inapplicable—changes limit applicability and exceedance evaluation (A) and how a missing Aldrin result is classified when no clear comparison basis exists (C).

candidates.locator: page 31, section fact_sheet, pollutants table, Chlordane row
candidates.computation_change_reason: Chlordane carries different numeric values across chronic aquatic, human health, daily-max, monthly-average, and load columns, including slight display differences (e.g., 0.18368676 vs 0.183686758). Choosing acute/chronic aquatic versus human-health versus concentration versus load as the governing limit changes the applicable threshold and any exceedance finding (A) and whether an unmatched monitoring result should be treated as comparable or left unresolved (C).

candidates.locator: page 31, section fact_sheet, pollutants table, Toxaphene row
candidates.computation_change_reason: Toxaphene lists both an acute aquatic limit (0.73) and a much lower chronic aquatic limit (0.00854357), plus separate human-health and load figures. Interpreting whether the acute, chronic, human-health, concentration, or load value governs compliance would materially change the applicable limit and any exceedance determination (A) and the semantics of missing or partial Toxaphene evidence (C).

candidates.locator: page 31, section fact_sheet, pollutants table, PESTICIDES AND PCBS subsection header
candidates.computation_change_reason: This subsection header groups Aldrin, Chlordane, Toxaphene, PCBs, and related compounds separately from the preceding pollutant rows.
